docs.title: JellyUX Homepage
docs.text:
A modular home screen engine for Jellyfin that replaces the default home page with a fully configurable widget system.

This site documents every widget and admin setting in detail. For installation instructions and a quick overview, see the README.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Configuration - global settings shared across widgets: cache TTLs, TMDb API keys, and TMDb list pagination.
  • Widgets (see the navigation menu) - one page per widget, grouped by category:
  • Native - built from your own Jellyfin library, no configuration needed beyond the shared parameters.
  • Admin - the administrator picks a specific value (a genre, an actor, a year, etc.).
  • Personalized - one row per rank, computed per user from their watch history.
  • Connected - powered by The Movie Database (TMDb), cross-referenced against your library.
  • Troubleshooting - known issues and their fixes.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
All settings below are found in Administration > Plugins > JellyUX Homepage, in three tabs: Settings, Sections and External sources. The page opens on the tab last used in the browser session, or on External sources when a TMDb list failed to refresh. Save writes every tab at once; a dot marks each tab with unsaved changes, and the Save bar says so.

Closing or reloading the browser tab with unsaved changes asks first. Going to another Jellyfin page cannot be stopped: the changes are kept for the browser session and shown again, with a Discard button, when you come back to the page, unless the saved configuration changed in the meantime.

docs.title: Modules
docs.text:
Each switch below turns one client module on or off. All are on by default. A disabled module is not loaded at all: its script is left out of the web client, so it costs nothing on any page. Changes apply at the next page reload. Unchecking Enable JellyUX Homepage leaves out every JellyUX script.

Switch What it adds Home tabs Watchlist, Progress, History and Statistics tabs on the home screen. Card watchlist button and infinite scroll Watchlist button on movie and series cards, and infinite scrolling on library pages. Single-season series The episodes of a single-season series shown directly on its page. Collections "Included In" section on detail pages, and sort controls on collection pages. Breadcrumb Library breadcrumb in the header of detail pages.

docs.title: Watchlist
docs.text: Remove watched titles from the watchlist (on by default): a movie leaves the watchlist when its playback finishes, a series when its last unwatched episode does. Marking a title as watched by hand never removes it. The watchlist is Jellyfin's "liked" list, which other plugins read too: Jellyfin Enhanced, for one, syncs it to Seerr, so a removed title also leaves the Seerr watchlist. Untick the setting to never change the list automatically.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text: Field Default Description Session cache TTL (minutes) 15 How long the home screen widget layout is cached per user, counted from when it was built. The first visit after that still shows the previous layout while the new one is built in the background. Saving the configuration clears this cache at once, so a lower value is never needed to see a configuration change. Reduce to see new library content sooner; increase to lower server load.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text: The Add a section bar sits at the top of the tab; the new section opens unfolded and is brought into view.

docs.title: Common per-widget parameters
docs.text:
Every widget section shares this set of fields, no matter its category:

Field Description Enabled Toggles the section on or off without removing it. Min items Section is hidden if fewer items than this are available. Max items Maximum number of items fetched per section, at most 100. View mode Card shape: Landscape, Portrait, or Square. Name Custom display name shown instead of the widget's default title. Not available for Personalized widgets, whose section names are generated per user (e.g. "Because you watched ...").

Widget pages in this site only document parameters that are specific to that widget, on top of this shared set.

docs.title: Sort order
docs.text:
Admin, Personalized (except Because You Watched) and Seasonal sections also have a Sort order: name, date added, release date or rating, in either direction, or Random. Sections saved before this setting existed keep their alphabetical order.

Random is drawn once a day for each user and section, from the items that user can see, and stays the same on every visit of that day; it changes at midnight (server time). Editing the section (its value, filters or Max items) draws again at once. Native sections (Continue Watching, Next Up, Recently Added), TMDb sections and Because You Watched keep their own order.

docs.title: Featured
docs.text:
Every section except My Media and the sections read from Jellyfin itself (Continue Watching, Next Up, Recently Added) has a Featured box. A featured section shows as a wide banner instead of a row of cards: one title at a time with its backdrop, logo, year, runtime, rating and tagline, Play and More info buttons, and the next titles beside it. It moves on every 8 seconds while it is on screen, and stops while the pointer or the keyboard focus is on it, in a hidden tab, or when the system asks for reduced motion. The pause button, the arrows, the left and right arrow keys and a swipe move it by hand.

The banner shows the section's titles that have a backdrop, at most 8 of them; with fewer than 3, the section shows all its cards instead (Min items counts every title, as for a row of cards). Minimum rating (None, 6, 7 or 8) keeps only the titles rated at least that much; it applies to a featured section only, a row of cards is never filtered. On a phone the image sits above the text; Android TV and other TV layouts keep the native home screen.

A "Top Rated" banner for one genre needs no special widget: add a Genre section, set its Sort order to rating (highest first), and check Featured.

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text: Field Description TMDb API Key Required for every TMDb-backed Connected widget. Leave empty if not needed. Accepted formats: a 32-character hexadecimal key (v3), or a v4 bearer token starting with ey. Not required for the Rewards widget, which uses Wikidata's free public data instead.

docs.title: TMDb Cache
docs.text:
The TMDb Cache section shows, per TMDb list type, the last refresh time and the number of cached items, plus a Refresh now button. Each page is roughly 20 items from TMDb, so setting "Pages: 3" fetches about 60 items for that list.

TMDb refresh interval (hours) (default 24): how often each TMDb list is refreshed, checked every hour. Increase to reduce external API calls; decrease for fresher content.

Field Applies to Default Pages Trending Movies, Trending Shows, On TV, Top Rated Movies, Top Rated Shows, Now Playing 1 (1-5) Min votes Top Rated Movies and Top Rated Shows (shared field) 200 Region Now Playing Default (all regions)

Note: Discover Movies has its own Pages field per configured section, independent of the global TMDb Lists pages above.

Refresh now also refreshes every configured Rewards section -- Rewards has no separate refresh button of its own, even though it is not TMDb data. It refreshes from the saved settings, so it is turned off while the tab has unsaved changes. Once started, the page follows the refresh and says when every list is done; if a refresh is already running, it says so.

When a list comes back empty because a TMDb request failed, its row says why (API key refused, rate-limited by TMDb, no answer in time, TMDb unreachable) and a warning at the top of the page says the same. The reason is cleared by the next refresh that returns items, or as soon as the API key is changed; it is kept in memory only, so a server restart clears it until the next refresh.

TMDb and Wikidata searches in the section editors, and the TMDb country and genre lists, answer within 8 seconds: past that, they show no result instead of waiting for the external service.

docs.title: User settings
docs.text: Each user finds a JellyUX block in Settings > Home: untick Use JellyUX to get Jellyfin's own home screen, tabs and pages back for that account, or untick a section to hide it from their own home screen. A hidden section keeps every setting chosen here; only its display is removed for that user. While JellyUX is on, the native Home screen section lists of that page are hidden, since the JellyUX sections replace them. Recently Added sections also follow the user's native Latest media choices (excluded libraries, hidden watched items).

docs.title: JellyUX tabs, or Custom Tabs tabs, open empty
docs.text:
JellyUX and Custom Tabs cannot be installed together. Both add tabs by patching the same home-html chunk through File Transformation, which runs only one transformation per file pattern: the plugin whose patch is applied keeps its panes, and the other plugin's buttons switch to the wrong, empty panes. The JellyUX configuration page warns about it whenever Custom Tabs is installed.

Fix: uninstall Custom Tabs by removing its folder from the Jellyfin plugins directory, then restart Jellyfin. Do not use Disable in Administration > Plugins for this: on Jellyfin 10.11 a disabled plugin is deleted at the next restart (see the README).

docs.title: "Cannot find module './'" in the browser console when opening a JellyUX tab
docs.text: Each click on a JellyUX tab logs one Uncaught (in promise) Error: Cannot find module './' in the browser console. It is harmless: the tab opens normally. Jellyfin Web loads a page controller for every home tab it is told about, and has one only for Home and Favorites; for any other tab (the JellyUX ones, or those of other plugins that add home tabs) that lookup fails, and Jellyfin does not catch the error. JellyUX leaves this native code path untouched rather than block it, since blocking it would also stop Jellyfin from pausing the Home tab while another tab is shown.

docs.title: Items hidden in Jellyfin Enhanced still show in some JellyUX sections
docs.text:
The JellyUX native sections (Continue Watching, Next Up, Recently Added Movies, Shows and Episodes) read the same Jellyfin routes as the native home page, so Jellyfin Enhanced hidden content, Remove from Continue Watching and Spoiler Guard apply to them exactly as on the native home page.

The other JellyUX sections (genres, collections, recommendations, TMDb and so on) come from the JellyUX server, which Jellyfin Enhanced does not filter. There, a hidden item is only removed by the Jellyfin Enhanced web script when it scans the page, which does not always happen on the first render, and Spoiler Guard does not replace episode titles.

docs.title: Plugin becomes unreachable (HTTP 500) after an update
docs.text: A simple Jellyfin restart may not be enough after updating the plugin. Do a full restart of the Jellyfin process itself (for example docker restart <container>) to clear the File Transformation plugin's static state.

docs.title: JellyUX sections don't appear on Jellyfin Media Player (Windows)
docs.text:
Jellyfin Media Player keeps an internal auto-connect cache (userWebClient in %LOCALAPPDATA%\JellyfinMediaPlayer\jellyfinmediaplayer.conf, main section) that isn't invalidated when you switch servers in the app. It keeps loading the web client, so every plugin (not just JellyUX), from the previously connected server, regardless of which server is currently selected.

Recommended fix: in the app's settings, use the Reset Saved Server button (shown automatically whenever a server is cached).

Fallback: edit jellyfinmediaplayer.conf and reset userWebClient to an empty string. Don't confuse this with the %LOCALAPPDATA%\Jellyfin Media Player cache folder (with spaces): clearing that one does not fix this specific issue, since it's an auto-connect cache, not a browser cache.

docs.title: "Forgot password?" button missing on the login page with ZestyTheme
docs.text: This is unrelated to JellyUX. ZestyTheme's theme.css intentionally hides .btnForgotPassword on the login page. To use password recovery, temporarily disable the ZestyTheme custom CSS (or remove the button's display: none override locally), recover the password, then re-enable the theme.

docs.title: TMDb requests stop working after a network outage
docs.text:
Connected widgets rely on TMDb's public API. After 3 consecutive network-level failures (not an invalid API key, which is reported separately), a circuit breaker opens and TMDb requests are skipped for 5 minutes rather than retried on every widget load. Look for a log line similar to:

TMDb circuit breaker opened after 3 consecutive failures; TMDb requests will be skipped for 5 minute(s).

This is expected behavior during a sustained TMDb outage and requires no action: normal requests resume automatically once the 5-minute window elapses and TMDb is reachable again.

docs.title: Sections don't appear even after clearing the browser cache and using incognito mode
docs.text:
JellyUX first repairs the browser side by itself: when the home page is rendered by a native copy of the patched chunks (typically a chunk the browser cached before the plugin was installed), it refetches the cached chunks, bypassing the browser cache, and reloads the page once, with a short "updating cached files" message. If the home page is still native after that reload, the message "a cache between this browser and the server (CDN or proxy) still serves an old copy" stays on screen: the stale copy then comes from outside the browser, as described below.

If the home page still shows native Jellyfin sections after installing or updating JellyUX, and this persists even in a private/incognito window or after fully clearing browser data, the cause is probably not the browser at all: a CDN or a caching reverse proxy in front of your Jellyfin server may be serving a cached copy of the patched chunk from before the install/update.

This was confirmed on a real deployment (TrueNAS app, Jellyfin behind an nginx reverse proxy, DNS managed through Cloudflare): the chunk containing loadSections was served with cf-cache-status: HIT at Cloudflare's edge, from before the plugin was installed. No amount of browser-side cache clearing can bust an edge/CDN cache, since it lives entirely outside the browser.

How to check: open your browser's developer tools (F12), go to the Network tab, reload the home page, find the request for the *.chunk.js file containing your home screen bundle, and inspect its response headers. A cf-cache-status: HIT (Cloudflare) or similar cache-hit header from any other CDN/reverse proxy confirms this is the cause rather than a plugin issue.

Fix: purge the cache at the CDN/proxy level, not the browser: - Cloudflare: dashboard > your zone > Caching > Configuration > Purge Cache (Purge Everything is simplest, since the chunk's filename hash changes on every Jellyfin Web update anyway). - nginx reverse proxy with proxy_cache: clear the configured cache path, or reload nginx if it was configured to bypass its own cache for the relevant location. - Other CDNs: use their equivalent cache purge/invalidation feature.

If you consistently run into this after every JellyUX update, consider adding a cache rule at your CDN/proxy that bypasses caching for *.chunk.js/*.bundle.js paths, or that purges automatically as part of your plugin update routine.

docs.title: All JellyUX settings are gone after a restart
docs.text:
When Jellyfin cannot read a plugin's configuration file (a truncated file after a full disk or a crash, for example), it replaces it with a blank configuration and saves it, without a log line. JellyUX keeps a copy of the configuration in its data folder (Jellyfin.Plugin.JuxHomepage/configuration.backup.xml under the Jellyfin data path), written each time the admin page is saved.

When the configuration comes back blank while such a copy exists, the admin page shows a warning with a Restore the saved configuration button, and the server logs a warning at startup. Nothing is restored on its own: restore the copy, or save the page to keep the blank configuration instead.

docs.title: JellyUX or File Transformation disappeared after a restart
docs.text:
On Jellyfin 10.11, Disable in Administration > Plugins can delete the plugin at the next restart (Jellyfin issue #15897, fixed in 12.0). At startup Jellyfin sorts the plugins by name and walks the list from the end: a disabled plugin found after an active one is deleted, and this is only logged at the Debug level. Whether it happens depends on the other plugins installed: on a server with Media Bar or TMDb Box Sets, both sort after JellyUX Homepage.

This applies to File Transformation too: once deleted, nothing injects JellyUX into the web client and the home page is native. The JellyUX admin page warns in its banner while JellyUX or File Transformation is disabled, before the restart: enable it again before restarting.

To turn JellyUX off, uncheck Enable JellyUX Homepage on its configuration page instead. If the plugin is already gone, reinstall it from the plugin catalog: its settings are kept, as the configuration file and the data folder are not deleted.

docs.title: Home page falls back to native rendering after a Jellyfin update
docs.text:
JellyUX patches a specific Jellyfin Web chunk to render its widgets. If Jellyfin Web's internal bundle changes shape (a "drift"), the patch may no longer apply, and a warning appears in the server logs:

Chunk <file>.chunk.js contains ',loadSections:' but the minified hook could not be resolved.

If you see this line, the home page falls back to Jellyfin's native rendering rather than showing a broken page. The admin page of JellyUX shows the same problem in its banner, and the home page shows "Jellyfin Web has changed: JellyUX went back to the native home screen" instead of reloading: purging a CDN or proxy cache does not help in this case. This is a known limitation of patching a third-party bundle that isn't part of JellyUX's public API. Check the project's GitHub Issues for a compatibility update, or open a new issue if none exists yet.

docs.title: A Rewards or Discover section shows nothing, or the admin page refuses to save a Rewards section
docs.text:
Before version 2.15, saving the admin page could drop the filters of a Rewards section (ceremony and category) and of a Discover section (person, keyword, company, and the genre when TMDb returned no genre list), even when nothing was changed. The update stops this from happening again, but it cannot bring back a filter that was already lost: the section stays empty until its filter is set again.

A Rewards section with neither a ceremony nor a category is now flagged on the admin page, which asks for one before saving, and the server logs this line at startup:

Rewards section '<id>' has no ceremony or category and shows nothing: set one on the JellyUX admin page.

Open the section on the admin page, search for its ceremony or category again, and save. A Discover section that lost its filters is not flagged, because a Discover section without a filter is valid: check its fields and set them again if needed.

docs.title: Actor
docs.text:
Category: Admin

Displays items featuring a specific actor chosen by the administrator. You can add multiple Actor sections, each pinned to a different actor.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters:

Field Description Value The actor this section shows, picked from an autocomplete list of people credited as actors in your library.

docs.title: Collection
docs.text:
Category: Admin

Displays items belonging to a specific collection (BoxSet) chosen by the administrator. You can add multiple Collection sections, each pinned to a different collection.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters:

Field Description Value The collection this section shows, picked from an autocomplete list of collections present in your library.

docs.title: Director
docs.text:
Category: Admin

Displays items directed by a specific director chosen by the administrator. You can add multiple Director sections, each pinned to a different director.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters:

Field Description Value The director this section shows, picked from an autocomplete list of people credited as directors in your library.

docs.title: Genre
docs.text:
Category: Admin

Displays items belonging to a specific genre chosen by the administrator. You can add multiple Genre sections, each pinned to a different genre.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters:

Field Description Value The genre this section shows, picked from an autocomplete list of genres present in your library.

docs.title: Recently Released
docs.text:
Category: Admin

Displays the latest releases of your library, newest release date first. Titles dated in the future are left out. The section needs no TMDb key: it reads your library only, in one query.

This preset is added disabled; turn it on from the admin page. You can add several Recently Released sections, for example one for movies and one for series.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters:

Field Description Show Movies and series (default for a new section), movies only, or series only.

docs.title: Studio
docs.text:
Category: Admin

Displays items from a specific studio chosen by the administrator. You can add multiple Studio sections, each pinned to a different studio.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters:

Field Description Value The studio this section shows, picked from an autocomplete list of studios present in your library.

docs.title: Tag
docs.text:
Category: Admin

Displays items matching a specific tag chosen by the administrator. You can add multiple Tag sections, each pinned to a different tag.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters:

Field Description Value The tag this section shows, picked from an autocomplete list of tags present in your library.

docs.title: Top Rated in Library
docs.text:
Category: Admin

Displays the best community-rated titles of your library, highest rating first. Unrated titles are left out. Not to be confused with the TMDb Top Rated Movies and Top Rated Shows sections, which list TMDb's ranking and only show the titles you own: this one ranks your own library, without a TMDb key, in one query.

This preset is added disabled; turn it on from the admin page.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters:

Field Description Show Movies and series (default for a new section), movies only, or series only.

docs.title: Year
docs.text:
Category: Admin

Displays items from a specific production year chosen by the administrator. You can add multiple Year sections, each pinned to a different year.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters:

Field Description Value The production year this section shows, picked from an autocomplete list of years present in your library.

docs.title: On TV
docs.text:
Category: Connected (TMDb)

Displays TV shows currently on the air (from TMDb's tv/on_the_air endpoint, which includes any show with an episode airing within the next 7 days) that are present in your local library.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Shares only the common parameters. Refresh frequency and page count are configured globally in the TMDb Cache settings.

docs.title: Discover Movies
docs.text:
Category: Connected (TMDb)

Displays movies matching an administrator-defined TMDb Discover filter, that are present in your local library. Unlike the other Connected widgets, each Discover Movies section has its own filter and its own independent cache: you can add several sections, each targeting a different combination of filters.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters, each section has its own filter block:

Field Description Genre Restrict results to a specific TMDb genre. Person Restrict results to movies featuring a specific person (actor or crew). Keyword Restrict results to movies matching a specific TMDb keyword. Company Restrict results to movies from a specific production company. Sort by TMDb sort order for the discover query. Defaults to popularity, descending. Year Restrict results to a specific primary release year. Min rating Minimum TMDb average vote (0-10) a movie must have. Min votes Minimum number of TMDb votes a movie must have, so a handful of extreme ratings don't skew the results. Defaults to 50. Pages How many pages of TMDb results to fetch for this section (1-5, roughly 20 movies per page). Defaults to 1. This is independent of the global TMDb Lists page counts used by the other Connected widgets.

All fields are optional except Pages; leave a field empty to not filter on it.

docs.title: Now Playing
docs.text:
Category: Connected (TMDb)

Displays movies currently playing in theatres, from TMDb, optionally filtered to a configured region, that are present in your local library.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Shares only the common parameters. Refresh frequency, page count, and the region filter are configured globally in the TMDb Cache settings.

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
Category: Connected (Wikidata)

Displays films from your local library that won an administrator-defined award. Unlike every other Connected widget, Rewards is not powered by TMDb: it queries Wikidata, a free, structured, community-maintained knowledge base, so no API key is required for this widget (contrast with the TMDb API Key needed by every other Connected widget).

Like Discover Movies, each Rewards section has its own filter and its own independent cache: add as many sections as you like, each targeting a different ceremony, category, or year.

docs.title: How targeting works
docs.text:
Every Rewards section is defined by up to three fields, combined as follows:

Field What it does Ceremony Every award category that belongs to this ceremony (e.g. every Academy Awards category: Best Picture, Best Director, Best Actor, ...). Category One specific award category, across every year it has been given out (e.g. only Best Picture, every year). Year Restricts to one specific edition/year. Only meaningful combined with Ceremony and/or Category -- a bare Year with nothing else is not a valid Wikidata query and returns nothing.

At least one of Ceremony or Category is required. The three fields combine into three practical configurations:

  1. Ceremony + Year -- "everything that won at one ceremony's edition" Ceremony: Academy Awards, Year: 2024 -> every film in your library that won any Academy Award category at the 2024 ceremony (Best Picture, Best Director, Best Actor, etc., whichever apply).
  2. Category only -- "every winner of one category, all years" Category: Academy Award for Best Picture, Year: (empty) -> every Best Picture winner in your library across every year Wikidata has data for.
  3. Category + Year -- "the winner of one category in one specific year" Category: Academy Award for Best Picture, Year: 2019 -> just that year's Best Picture winner, if it's in your library.

Ceremony and Category can also be combined together, but this is rarely useful since Category alone already pins down the ceremony (a category like "Academy Award for Best Picture" only ever belongs to one ceremony).

docs.title: Searching for a Ceremony or Category
docs.text:
Both fields autocomplete against Wikidata as you type, proxied through the Jellyfin server (a compliant identification header is required by Wikidata and cannot be set from a browser, so the search cannot run client-side).

Wikidata's search matches broadly across its entire database, not just awards -- a short, generic query like "Academy" will surface unrelated entities too (a school, a video game, an unrelated film literally titled "Academy"). Type the full, specific name for clean results, e.g.:

  • Academy Awards (not Academy) for the Ceremony field
  • Academy Award for Best Picture (not Best Picture) for the Category field
  • César Award for Best Film for a French example

Pick the entry whose description confirms what you meant (e.g. "annual awards for cinematic achievements" for the Academy Awards ceremony, "annual award from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences" for the Best Picture category).

docs.title: Worked examples
docs.text:
"Films from your library that won an Oscar in 2024" - Ceremony: Academy Awards - Category: (empty) - Year: 2024

"Every Best Picture winner you own, any year" - Ceremony: (empty) - Category: Academy Award for Best Picture - Year: (empty)

"This specific year's César for Best Film, if you own it" - Ceremony: (empty) - Category: César Award for Best Film - Year: 2016

docs.title: Data coverage
docs.text:
Wikidata's award data is community-maintained and not guaranteed to be complete for every ceremony and year. Well-established, high-profile ceremonies (e.g. the Academy Awards) tend to have excellent, continuous coverage; smaller or more regional ceremonies may have real, confirmed gaps for some years (the César Award for Best Film, for example, is missing a small number of years). If a configured combination shows no section on the home screen, it can mean one of three things, roughly in order of likelihood:

  1. You don't own any of the matching films -- the query found winners, none are in your library. This is normal and expected, not an error.
  2. Wikidata genuinely has no data for that exact combination (a real gap in its records).
  3. A transient failure reached out to Wikidata and got no answer that time. This widget deliberately does not retry aggressively (see below) -- click Refresh now again, or wait for the next scheduled refresh.

To tell these apart, check Dashboard > Logs right after a refresh for a line from Jellyfin.Plugin.JuxHomepage.Rewards.RewardsCacheService: it reports how many items were fetched from Wikidata and how many matched your local library. 6 item(s), 1 matched means Wikidata found 6 winners and only 1 is in your library (case 1, expected); 0 items with no library match at all means either case 2 or 3 -- a preceding warning from WikidataApiClient in the same log, if present, confirms case 3 (a network failure or rate limit).

docs.title: Refreshing
docs.text: Rewards data refreshes automatically once a week (rather than daily like TMDb data -- award results for a given ceremony change at most once a year, so a more frequent refresh would only add unnecessary load on Wikidata's public service). It can also be refreshed immediately: Rewards shares the Refresh now button in the TMDb Cache section of the admin panel with every TMDb-backed widget -- there is no separate Rewards-only refresh button.

docs.title: Seasonal
docs.text:
Category: Admin

Displays items from your local library during a recurring, admin-configured date window (e.g. Halloween, Christmas), filtered by genres and/or tags. Like the other Admin widgets, Seasonal reads only your library (no TMDb or Wikidata call, no API key needed), but it has its own editor in the admin panel (theme, dates, genres, tags) instead of the single-value picker the other Admin widgets share.

The plugin ships with seven disabled-by-default presets over four seasons (Halloween, Christmas, Valentine's Day, New Year); enable the ones you want, or add your own custom Seasonal section with any date window, theme, and genre/tag filter. As in KefinTweaks, a season can have several sections, each with its own filter.

A section outside its configured date window returns no items and is automatically hidden from the home screen, the same generic "not enough items" behavior every widget already relies on -- there is no separate "hide when out of season" setting to configure. A section with neither a genre nor a tag is hidden too: without a filter it would show your whole library.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters:

Field Description Theme An optional theme label (Halloween, Christmas, Valentine's Day, New Year, or none). It has no visual effect today: it is a label for your own organization, kept on the section for a future per-theme look. Start date / End date The recurring MM-DD window during which this section is shown (e.g. 10-01 to 10-31 for Halloween). A window whose end date is earlier than its start date is treated as wrapping across the new year (e.g. 12-26 to 01-06). Genres Genres of your library, separated by \| (e.g. Horror\|Horreur): a title with any of them matches. Genre names follow the language of your metadata, so list each spelling your library uses. Tags Tags of your library, separated by \|: a title with any of them matches. When both genres and tags are set, a title needs one of each.

docs.title: Presets
docs.text:
Preset Default window Default theme Filter Halloween October 1 - October 31 Halloween tag halloween Halloween Horror October 1 - October 31 Halloween genres Horror\|Horreur Halloween Thrillers October 1 - October 31 Halloween genre Thriller Christmas December 1 - December 25 Christmas tag christmas Valentine's Day February 7 - February 14 Valentine's Day tag valentine's day Valentine's Romance February 7 - February 14 Valentine's Day genre Romance New Year December 26 - January 6 New Year tag new year's eve

The tags are TMDb keyword names, the tags Jellyfin writes from TMDb metadata. Genre names follow the language of your metadata: the Horror preset lists the English and the French name; add your own spelling if your library uses another language. A preset whose filter matches fewer titles than its minimum stays hidden. Each preset ships disabled; enable the ones you want and adjust the dates or the filters to fit your library and timezone.

When upgrading, a preset section you never gave a filter receives the filter of its preset (it used to show the whole library); a section you filtered yourself is left unchanged.

A preset section shows its name in each user's language (English or French today) until you type a name of your own; on upgrade, a preset still carrying its original English name switches to the translated one.

docs.title: Top Rated Movies
docs.text:
Category: Connected (TMDb)

Displays all-time top rated movies from TMDb (filtered by a minimum vote count, so obscure titles with a handful of 10/10 votes don't crowd out well-established favorites) that are present in your local library.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Shares only the common parameters. Refresh frequency, page count, and the minimum vote count threshold are configured globally in the TMDb Cache settings (the "Min votes" field is shared with Top Rated Shows).

docs.title: Watchlist
docs.text:
Category: Native

The user's Watchlist -- items marked via the bookmark toggle on card overlays, the item detail page, or the "More" menu (see the Watchlist tab). Reuses the exact same Likes-based query as the Watchlist tab itself, so the two always stay in sync.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Shares only the common parameters. No widget-specific settings.

docs.title: Because You Watched
docs.text:
Category: Personalized

Displays movies related to a film the requesting user recently watched, sharing at least one genre with that reference film.

docs.title: How ranking works
docs.text: Each Because You Watched section you add gets a rank, based on the order the sections were added. At render time, each user's recently watched films are ranked from their own watch history, and each section is based on the film at its rank for that user: rank 1 uses their most recently watched film, rank 2 uses their second most recently watched film, and so on. If a user doesn't have enough recently watched films to fill every configured rank, the extra sections are simply not shown for that user.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters:

Field Description Exclude already watched When enabled, titles the user has already watched are not recommended.

Note: Personalized widgets don't have a custom name field. Section names are generated per user (for example "Because you watched ...").

docs.title: Favorite Actor
docs.text:
Category: Personalized

Displays movies featuring the requesting user's favorite actors, derived from their watch history.

docs.title: How ranking works
docs.text: Each Favorite Actor section you add gets a rank, based on the order the sections were added. At render time, each user's actors are scored from their own watch history, and each section shows the actor at its rank for that user: rank 1 shows their single most-watched actor, rank 2 shows their second most-watched actor, and so on. If a user doesn't have enough distinct actors to fill every configured rank, the extra sections are simply not shown for that user.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters:

Field Description Exclude already watched When enabled, titles the user has already watched are not recommended.

Note: Personalized widgets don't have a custom name field. Section names are generated per user.

docs.title: On a small library
docs.text: An actor match is narrow -- usually just a handful of titles per person, unlike a genre match. With Exclude already watched on, a section only shows if enough unwatched titles from that actor remain; if a user has already watched most or all of what the library owns from their top-scored actor, there may be nothing left to recommend, and the section is hidden rather than shown empty. This is expected behavior, not a bug -- it becomes less noticeable as the library grows. If it's too aggressive on a smaller library, either disable Exclude already watched for this widget or lower Min items.

docs.text:

docs.title: How ranking works
docs.text: Each Favorite Director section you add gets a rank, based on the order the sections were added. At render time, each user's directors are scored from their own watch history, and each section shows the director at its rank for that user: rank 1 shows their single most-watched director, rank 2 shows their second most-watched director, and so on. If a user doesn't have enough distinct directors to fill every configured rank, the extra sections are simply not shown for that user.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters:

Field Description Exclude already watched When enabled, titles the user has already watched are not recommended.

Note: Personalized widgets don't have a custom name field. Section names are generated per user.

docs.title: On a small library
docs.text: A director match is narrow -- usually just a handful of titles per person, unlike a genre match. With Exclude already watched on, a section only shows if enough unwatched titles from that director remain; if a user has already watched most or all of what the library owns from their top-scored director, there may be nothing left to recommend, and the section is hidden rather than shown empty. This is expected behavior, not a bug -- it becomes less noticeable as the library grows. If it's too aggressive on a smaller library, either disable Exclude already watched for this widget or lower Min items.

docs.title: Favorite Genre
docs.text:
Category: Personalized

Displays items from the requesting user's favorite genres, derived from their watch history.

docs.title: How ranking works
docs.text: Each Favorite Genre section you add gets a rank, based on the order the sections were added (the first section is rank 1, the second is rank 2, and so on). At render time, each user's genres are scored from their own watch history, and each section shows the genre at its rank for that user: rank 1 shows their single most-watched genre, rank 2 shows their second most-watched genre, and so on. If a user doesn't have enough distinct genres to fill every configured rank, the extra sections are simply not shown for that user, rather than repeating an already-shown genre.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
In addition to the common parameters:

Field Description Exclude already watched When enabled, titles the user has already watched are not recommended.

Note: Personalized widgets don't have a custom name field. Section names are generated per user (for example "Because you watched ...").

docs.title: On a small library
docs.text: With Exclude already watched on, a section only shows if enough unwatched titles in that genre remain. A genre match is broad, so this is rarely an issue -- but on a small library, or for a genre the user has watched most of already, the section may be hidden rather than shown empty. See Favorite Actor for the same behavior in its narrower, more noticeable form.
